_comment: C0-5 body translation for coding/jules. Keys align with build.mjs: axes by axis key; sections/sectionTitles by the Chinese headings of extraSections; runs/unknowns/related/sources by index alignment.
_rules: 0) Keep ** emphasis, `code`, links and table structure, block-for-block with the Chinese side.
1) Official English quotes stay verbatim; Chinese-rendered paraphrases of official wording are marked (translated) on the English side — never fabricate English originals.
2) Do not upgrade 'unverified / not stated officially' semantics; the translation changes no facts.

axes.model_access:
**The model is vendor-assigned; you cannot choose it.**

The only place the readable official pages name a model is the GA launch page. It says Jules uses the advanced reasoning capabilities of Gemini 2.5 Pro. The Google One plan page writes, for the Ultra tier, Jules "access to latest models", meaning **higher tiers get newer models**.

Which tier maps to which model is not written officially.

(developers.google.com/jules/api and the Google One AI plans page checked.)

**Official wording**: "Jules now uses the advanced thinking capabilities of Gemini 2.5 Pro"

This is the exact opposite of the IDE / CLI classes. Those usually offer a selection surface like `/model`, while **the vendor-cloud form takes the whole "pick a model" decision away**.
axes.runtime:
**Tasks run on Google's cloud VMs; nothing is installed locally.**

Each task gets a **brand-new** cloud VM: inside it Jules clones your repo, installs dependencies, and changes code.

**Official FAQ wording**: "Each task runs in a fresh virtual machine where Jules clones your repo, installs dependencies, and makes changes based on your prompt"
**The official GA launch page lists this as a selling point**: "Tasks run inside a cloud VM, enabling concurrent execution"

Besides the web app (jules.google), there are two more entry points: the Jules REST API (`jules.googleapis.com/v1alpha`) and the Jules Tools CLI. **But execution always happens on the vendor cloud; clients only submit and observe.**
axes.local_files:
**By default it is fully isolated from your local machine.**

Jules only clones repos and works inside the cloud VM; it never touches files on your machine. This VM **has internet access** — which is both a capability and a risk surface.

**Official FAQ**: the VM is "executed in a secure, cloud-based virtual machine (VM) with internet access", and users are told to "treat the environment with the same security precautions you would for any public or shared compute surface".
**The official pages also warn**: do not commit secrets, tokens and the like into the repo.

Which repos are visible to Jules is decided by the authorization scope of the Jules GitHub app (the FAQ points to GitHub's applications settings for per-repo adjustment).
axes.background:
**This is its thickest dimension; the official pages define it as "asynchronous" throughout.**

Jules operates asynchronously, allowing you to focus on other tasks while it works in the background

You can leave the app after submitting a task

Just turn on notifications. **Failed tasks retry automatically.**

Jules will retry automatically

The official 2025-12-10 update adds two proactive capabilities:

- **Suggested Tasks** — proactively scans code and proposes improvements across up to five repos, starting with `#todos`
- **Scheduled Tasks** — runs automatically at your defined cadence, e.g. dependency checks, weekly routines

Scheduled Tasks ... you can now define the cadence and Jules will perform the task at that time

**Concurrent task counts vary by subscription tier** (concrete numbers live on the official plan page; this site does not store them per the D9 rule).
axes.tools:
**The tool surface centers on execution capability inside the cloud VM plus GitHub integration.**

The official FAQ and GA page confirm the VM's execution capabilities: installing dependencies, running tests, building via setup scripts. Supported languages are JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Rust.

language agnostic but works best with

(in practice it depends on what is installed in the VM.)

**Long-running processes are not supported** — things like `npm run dev` will not run.

Long-running processes like dev servers or watch scripts aren't currently supported in setup scripts

There is also front-end verification: run scripts inside the VM and get screenshots back. See the web-app testing notes on the official launch page.

**Whether Jules supports connecting MCP servers: not stated officially.**

(developers.google.com/jules/api and the official FAQ page checked.)
axes.context:
**Session / Activity is the unit of context.**

Session — A continuous unit of work within a specific context, similar to a chat session. A session is initiated with a prompt and a source

Activity — A single unit of work within a Session

One Session contains multiple activities from both the user and the agent, e.g. plan generation, messages, progress updates.

In other words, **for programmatic use the context is the pollable "session + activity" state stream**, not a one-shot conversation. Across tasks, the official pages offer **environment snapshot** reuse:

reusing previous setups so new tasks run faster

**Context-window size and the concrete implementation of long-term memory — no numbers given on the readable official pages; not stated officially.**

(Jules API page and official FAQ page checked.)
axes.permissions:
**The core of approval is "plan approval", and the API and web defaults differ.**

By default, sessions created through the API will have their plans automatically approved. If you want to create a session that requires explicit plan approval, set the `requirePlanApproval` field to `true`

The web default is:

**Official wording**: "Prompt a task and approve Jules' plan"

**i.e. the programmatic entry skips human approval by default; it must be explicitly turned on.**

How code lands is decided by the `automationMode` set when creating the session — only `AUTO_CREATE_PR` opens a PR automatically.

The `automationMode` field is optional. By default, no PR will be automatically created

Repo access follows the authorization scope of the Jules GitHub app.

**Privacy stance: the official FAQ states clearly it does not train on private repo content.**

Jules does not train on private repository content

**Quota boundary**: the concrete task counts for the free tier and Pro / Ultra are not listed on the readable official pages (see the official plan page). But the point that **"quota is counted per task, not per token"** can be read from the official API concept (session is the task unit).
axes.fit:
The work the official pages scope for it is concrete: hand a task description to a GitHub repo and it does these things:

- **Official wording**: "fix bugs, update dependencies, migrate code, and add new features"
- Delivery form **official wording**: "test verified patches", "Open PRs with runnable code and test results"

So it **fits self-contained, verifiable work**: fixing a clear bug, bumping a dependency, adding tests, migrating code snippets, small-scope new features.
It **does not fit**: real-time shell work and high-frequency change-as-it-runs interaction — for that, the CLI / IDE forms in this section are better. It also does not fit vague, architecture-level tasks needing heavy clarification. The official FAQ itself lists "vague prompts" among common causes of task failure.

sections.异步流程与计划审批（本次核验重点）:
The official REST docs spell the flow out clearly, and one point is the easiest to misread:

**Official wording**: By default, sessions created through the API will have their plans
**Official wording**: automatically approved. If you want to create a session that requires
**Official wording**: explicit plan approval, set the `requirePlanApproval` field to `true`.

**i.e.: tasks created via the API have their plans auto-approved by default; human gating must be explicitly turned on.** The web default is "Prompt a task and approve Jules' plan".

PR generation likewise needs an explicit switch:

**Official wording**: The `automationMode` field is optional. By default, no PR will be
**Official wording**: automatically created.

Only `AUTO_CREATE_PR` opens PRs automatically.

Progress comes back as an activity stream. Related API methods and event names:

**Methods**: `sessions/{id}:approvePlan`, `sessions`, `sessions/{id}:sendMessage`
**Events**: `planGenerated` / `progressUpdated` / `sessionCompleted`
**Artifacts**: `bashOutput`, `changeSet` (gitPatch)
sections.核验说明:
Basis for `confidence: partial`: this round verified the official GA launch page, the Google One plan page, the Jules API and its REST reference, the official FAQ page, and two official blog updates.

**The gaps fall into two classes, and these two classes genuinely are absent from the readable official pages:**

- "Numbers": per-tier daily task counts and concurrency (the jules.google pricing page is JS-rendered and could not be captured)
- "Model mapping": the current default model and which model each tier maps to
- Also: whether MCP is supported

Per this site's rules these are recorded as "not stated officially", with the checked pages listed — **no guessing.**

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md).

**Suggested measurement** (three items, all pointing at what the readable official pages do not give):

- **The real behavior of the plan-approval switch** — the API defaults to auto-approve, the web requires approval; the two defaults differ
- **Whether tasks keep running after you close the browser**, and whether a PR really gets opened on completion
- **How much the free tier and Pro tier actually differ in task counts** — that number is not on the official pages; only measurement can confirm it
